title: `ExactCFbend` ignores the skew dipole `k_skew[0]`
summary: `ExactCFbend` leaves the skew-dipole coefficient `k_skew[0]` out of its orbital kick, so a skew dipole produces no vertical steering. title: `RFCavity` spin transport rotates spin without a field and uses `sqrt(1+pt²)` for βγ
summary: With spin tracking enabled (experimental in ImpactX), `RFCavity` rotates the spin incorrectly: one spin-coupling term omits the on-axis field profile, and two divide by √(1 + γ²) instead of the reference momentum βγ. title: `DipEdge(modify_ref_part=True)` deflects the reference by the beam-normalized kick
summary: With the nonlinear `DipEdge` model and `modify_ref_part=True`, ImpactX adds the fringe kick, normalized to the reference momentum P₀, directly to the reference particle's `px`, which is stored in units of mc. title: Soft-edge elements and their `reverse()` do not cancel in a lattice
summary: A `SoftQuadrupole`, `SoftSolenoid` or `RFCavity` followed by its `reverse()` copy in a lattice does not return particles to their initial coordinates, although the manual documents `reverse()` as undoing the original element. Lattice tracking resets the field-profile origin at each element, so the reversed element (negative `ds`) integrates outside its field profile; with a flat profile it reduces to a drift of length −`ds`. Pushing the reversed element directly, which keeps the forward element's profile origin, closes the round trip to 2.1e-16. title: Periodic `PolygonAperture` mirrors asymmetric polygons
summary: A `PolygonAperture` with a nonzero period `repeat_x` (or `repeat_y`) folds coordinates into the central cell through their absolute value, which mirrors every negative coordinate. For a polygon that is not symmetric about x = 0 (or y = 0), particles inside the aperture are removed and particles whose mirror image lies inside it pass, whereas repeating the aperture with a period must leave a point already in the central period unchanged. title: `ExactCFbend` octupole and decapole kicks lose all precision at small curvature
summary: `ExactCFbend` evaluates its octupole and decapole kicks as differences of order-one terms in 1 + x/`rc` and then multiplies them by powers of the bend radius `rc`, so rounding dominates at small curvature: the error scales as ε·`rc`³·k₃ for the octupole and ε·`rc`⁴·k₄ for the decapole, with k₃ and k₄ their coefficients and ε the double-precision machine epsilon. title: Integer factorial overflow corrupts multipole normalization

title: Built-in H⁻ species has the wrong magnetic-anomaly sign
summary: With spin tracking enabled (experimental in ImpactX), the built-in `Hminus` species uses the proton's magnetic anomaly a = 1.793 together with its negative charge, which reverses the ion's magnetic moment and its spin precession. title: Touschek Monte Carlo diagnostic omits sampled angular width
summary: `TouschekScatter` samples the polar scattering angle θ uniformly between `theta_min` and `theta_max` and the azimuth over π, but always uses the Monte Carlo volume π² instead of π·(θₘₐₓ − θₘᵢₙ). title: All-lost tracking calls freeze wake history
summary: `WakeTracker.track` returns early when no particle is alive, before advancing the stored wake-source history, so a turn in which the whole bunch is lost does not age the history. title: B&M applies an extra beta factor to momentum dispersion
summary: `BjorkenMtingwaIBS`, the Bjorken–Mtingwa model of intrabeam-scattering growth rates, multiplies the dispersions and their slopes in both planes by the relativistic reference speed β₀. title: Zero horizontal dispersion invariant creates a NaN B&M rate
summary: `BjorkenMtingwaIBS` divides by the horizontal dispersion invariant Hₓ, which is zero where both the dispersion `dx` and its slope `dpx` vanish, so one such sampled location makes the horizontal growth rate Kₓ NaN. For protons at reference speed β₀ = 0.45 (in units of c) with zero dispersion, Kₓ is NaN instead of −2.872 × 10⁻³ s⁻¹; in a three-segment line with only one zero-invariant location, it is NaN instead of −7.397 × 10⁻⁴ s⁻¹. NumPy emits division warnings and the other planes stay finite; a nonzero `dpx` avoids the singularity even when `dx` = 0.

title: Single-harmonic longitudinal generation uses proton mass for other species
summary: With `engine='single-rf-harmonic'`, `generate_longitudinal_coordinates` samples the energy coordinate p_τ (`ptau`) for the requested reference particle, but converts it to the relative momentum deviation δ (`delta`) through a temporary `Particles` built without the reference mass, so the default proton mass is used for every species. title: Checkpoint loading restores RNG words onto reordered particle coordinates
summary: On CPU, loading a checkpoint with `Particles.from_dict(load_rng_state=True)` and default options reorders the coordinates into active-then-lost order but restores the saved random-number-generator (RNG) words in their original slot order. title: Manager.copy disconnects containers from dependency tasks
summary: In Xdeps, the dependency-graph library behind Xtrack's deferred expressions, `Manager.copy` deep-copies the containers, the tasks (expressions computing dependent values) and the dependency maps separately, so the returned containers and tasks refer to different copies and references into the copy stay bound to a hidden manager. `Manager.set_value` promises to update the target and run its dependent tasks, and `copy.deepcopy` of the whole manager keeps the copied graph connected. title: CPU linked-array views bypass dependent-state updates
summary: Writing through a shared CPU slice of `Particles.delta` changes the relative momentum deviation δ without updating the dependent energy and momentum fields, so subsequent tracking uses inconsistent coordinates. title: Sagan tracking guide uses nonexistent names
summary: The `SaganCavity` tracking guide's examples fail when copied, because they use the keyword `num_cells`, the nonexistent enum name `PhaseReference`, and `zero_phase` as a `SaganCavity` keyword. The constructor and export list instead provide `n_cells` and `PhaseRef`, and `zero_phase` belongs to the cavity element's `RFParams`. The guide's two-cell call with active length 1.600 m raises `MethodError`, while `SaganCavity(n_cells=2, L_active=1.6)` succeeds; passing `zero_phase` to that constructor also raises `MethodError`. The physics guide repeats the wrong cell-count keyword.

title: Stale docstrings: `Bunch` callback signature, `SciBmadStandard` "Yoshida"
summary: Two docstrings describe interfaces that do not exist: the `Bunch` docstring prescribes a three-argument callback that tracking cannot call, and the `SciBmadStandard` docstring names a nonexistent `Yoshida` integrator. The callback call site passes nine arguments, so a callback written as documented, `callback(coords, ds_step, g)`, raises `MethodError`. The default method actually uses `Symplectic` with keyword `n_steps`, at order 2 for exact bodies and order 4 otherwise, not `Yoshida(order=4, num_steps=1)`.

title: `sincu`/`sinhcu` use the two-term series for arguments up to 0.004 in magnitude in Float64
summary: In Float64 the helpers `sincu` (sin x / x) and `sinhcu` (sinh x / x) use the two-term series 1 ∓ x²/6 for |x| up to 0.004000, although their docstrings promise accuracy near the origin, which limits accuracy for weak elements. High-precision references and the omitted x⁴/120 term establish the error: at x = 0.003900 each helper is low by 1.928 × 10⁻¹², and the derivative of `sincu` has relative error 1.521 × 10⁻⁶. In a 0.7300 m `Exact()` bend of angle 0.002920 rad, the longitudinal coordinate differs from an independent high-precision circular trajectory by 4.221 × 10⁻¹³ m. The error occurs for both signs of x; it limits tight convergence comparisons and is negligible for ordinary tracking.

title: `BendKick` applies a straight dipole's other multipoles unrotated in the dipole's frame
summary: With an explicit `BendKick` method, a tilted, skew or negative straight dipole applies its other multipoles in the wrong frame, changing orbit and spin transport. Rotation covariance (a tilted magnet must equal the untilted one between coordinate rotations) and independent Lorentz-force integration establish the correct map. For a proton with reference momentum p₀c = 2mc², twice its rest energy, in a 0.2000 m dipole of normalized strength 0.3000 m⁻¹ with sextupole strength 0.8000 m⁻³, both tilted by 0.3700 rad, the spin quaternion is off by up to 6.122 × 10⁻⁵ per component instead of 0. The default method avoids this mixed-multipole orbital error, but tilted or skew pure straight dipoles get incorrect radiation damping on the default path; curved bends are unaffected.

title: Builders skip the frame rotation at a nominally zero angle and drop its derivative
summary: Differentiating tracking with respect to a tilt, skew strength or bend-face angle whose nominal value is zero can silently discard its first-order response. Finite differences and the equivalent alignment rotation establish the response: for a 5.000 GeV electron in a 0.2000 m quadrupole of normalized strength 0.5000 m⁻², the derivative of the exit normalized vertical momentum with respect to `tilt1` is 0 instead of −2.988 × 10⁻³ rad⁻¹ under both GTPSA and ForwardDiff. GTPSA, the truncated power series package behind SciBmad's Taylor maps, loses these derivatives consistently; ForwardDiff's failure depends on the sign of the differentiated variable. Source inspection extends the affected tests to combined-function and implicit bend builders; ordinary floating-point tracking and alignment tilts are unaffected.

title: Callback out/in transforms change momentum in a time-dependent potential
summary: A callback whose coordinate transforms only take particles out for observation and back in changes their momentum in a time-dependent scalar potential. The observer contract requires an unchanged trajectory, and an independent mass-shell calculation identifies an incorrect time in the inward conversion. For a proton in a 0.6000 m element with dimensionless potential φ = κct·16(s/L)²(1 − s/L)², where κ = 0.3000 m⁻¹, c is light speed, t is time, s is position and L is the element length, the final relative momentum offset is 0.1993 instead of 0.1835. Constant-potential and no-op-callback controls agree with tracking without an observer; the error requires both the coordinate transforms and time dependence.

title: Zero alignment applies a bend's reference roll twice
summary: Adding an explicit zero `AlignmentParams` group to a bend with a reference roll changes its orbit; at zero reference curvature the roll is applied twice. Zero alignment must preserve transport, and an independent Lorentz-force trajectory agrees with the unaligned map at the intended roll and with the aligned map at twice that roll. For a 0.1900 m straight-reference bend with normalized strength −0.1700 m⁻¹ and reference roll 0.01500 rad, the kick in normalized vertical momentum is 9.689 × 10⁻⁴ instead of 4.845 × 10⁻⁴. This occurs with `Exact`, `Symplectic` and the default method, and bends with finite curvature also change under zero alignment; omitting or ignoring the alignment group restores the unaligned map.

title: Stored zero dipole strength corrupts coordinates at bend faces
summary: Storing an explicit zero dipole strength in a bend with an enabled nonzero face angle produces NaN coordinates and can mark particles lost. With zero field each particle must follow a straight line to the reference exit plane, as an independent high-precision geometry calculation confirms. Across four geometries with lengths 0.3000–1.100 m and curvatures −0.2500 to 0.4000 m⁻¹, all 24 default-method cases lose all 16 particles instead of transporting them with finite coordinates. Omitting the field entry, setting both face angles to zero, disabling fringes or selecting `Exact()` preserves every particle; in mixed-strength batches exactly the zero-strength lanes fail.

title: Neutron g_spin conflicts with its own-mass normalization contract
summary: The neutron and antineutron `g_spin` values are normalized to the nuclear magneton, which uses the proton mass, although the accessor promises normalization to each particle's own mass. Combining the returned value with the documented formula therefore disagrees with the tabulated magnetic moment, and converting by the neutron-to-proton mass ratio restores agreement. With CODATA 2022 active, neutron `g_spin` with `signed=true` is −3.826 instead of the own-mass value −3.831, implying a gyromagnetic ratio of −1.830 × 10⁸ instead of −1.832 × 10⁸ s⁻¹ T⁻¹, a 0.1377% magnitude error. Antineutron signs reverse with the same fractional error; charged species agree.

title: Coasting `twiss` ignores `delta0`; `a_initial` runs ignore `delta0` and `v0`
summary: For a coasting beam (RF off), `twiss(delta0=δ₀)` finds the closed orbit at the momentum offset δ₀ but tracks the map from δ = 0, and a run started from an initial normalizing map `a_initial` ignores both `delta0` and `v0`. Thin-lens transfer matrices and Jacobians of tracking at δ₀ give the correct optics: for 1 GeV/c electrons in a thin-quadrupole cell at δ₀ = 0.01, `twiss` returns the tune q₁ = 0.1436 and β₁ = 3.441 m instead of 0.1422 and 3.421 m, and `pz` = 0. In a checked ring with dispersion the tabulated orbit does not close and the spin tune is taken at δ = 0. Periodic optics with RF on are unaffected, but `a_initial` still bypasses `v0`.

title: Scalar `d<col>_<n>` returns f⁽ⁿ⁾/n, not the nth derivative
summary: A `twiss` chromatic derivative column `d<col>_<n>` with scalar output, such as `dx_2` or `dbeta1_2`, returns the nth derivative with respect to the momentum offset δ divided by n. The docstring promises the nth derivative itself, n! times the stored Taylor coefficient, which the `as_taylor_series=true` output, nested ForwardDiff and finite differences of tracking all give. For a thin-quadrupole cell with `chrom=4`, `dbeta1_2` is 2.585 m instead of 5.171 m, and `dbeta1_3` is −7.457 m instead of −22.37 m. Every scalar column of order 2 and higher is low by exactly n; first-order columns such as `dx` and `dbeta1` are correct.

title: `h<ijkl>` columns are degree-weighted, and the scalar and Taylor paths disagree
summary: The `twiss` resonance-driving-term columns `h<ijkl>`, the Bengtsson coefficients of the one-turn Lie generator h, are scaled by a monomial-dependent factor, so scalar and Taylor-series outputs disagree. For a thin octupole of integrated strength K3L the documented coefficient is `h2200` = K3L β²/16, and the normal-form tune slope with amplitude independently confirms this normalization. With K3L = 1000 m⁻³ in a thin-quadrupole cell, the octupole's `h2200` increment is 2961 m⁻¹ in scalar output and 1480 m⁻¹ in Taylor output instead of 740.1 m⁻¹, and a thin sextupole gives `h3000` three times its expected value. Scalar coefficients carry the monomial degree as a factor, Taylor coefficients the last contributing exponent, and the chromatic `dh…_n` columns inherit the error.

title: Linear De Moivre `B`/`E` use columns of A⁻¹ instead of rows
summary: In its linear branch (expansion order 1), `twiss` builds the De Moivre matrices `B` and `E`, which split the one-turn matrix and the beam moments by mode, from columns of A⁻¹, the inverse normalizing matrix, instead of its rows. In an uncoupled plane the documented definition gives E₁ = [β −α; −α γ], and the corresponding B₁ matches a tracked one-turn Jacobian to 1.8e-15. For a thin-quadrupole cell with β = 3.441 m and α = −1.376, the returned E₁[1,2] and E₁[2,1] are 0 and 1.776 instead of 1.376, and E₁[2,2] is 0.2906 m⁻¹ instead of 0.8412 m⁻¹. The horizontal beam-size term used by `dynamic_aperture` stays correct in uncoupled lattices; by source algebra, its vertical mode-1 term and coupled lattices are wrong.

title: Map-valued `E1..E3` throw `UndefVarError: nj_mat`
summary: Requesting the De Moivre matrix `E1` from coasting `twiss` above order 1, such as `twiss(chrom=2)`, throws `UndefVarError: nj_mat` instead of returning the documented matrix, because its map-valued branch reads undefined variables. By source inspection, `E1` and `E2` fail in higher-order coasting runs, and `E1`–`E3` in higher-order RF runs with knob parameters. Order-1 optics and RF optics without knobs take a separate linear branch; `E3` is explicitly unavailable for coasting beams.

title: Summary `alphac` (momentum compaction) equals the slip factor `etac`
summary: The `twiss` summary value `alphac`, labelled the momentum compaction α_p = (1/C) dC/dδ (C the orbit length, δ the relative momentum offset), is computed from the coordinate slip, like the slip factor `etac`. For coasting beams on momentum whose closed orbit has zero longitudinal advance, `alphac` equals `etac` and is low by 1/γ² (γ the Lorentz factor). For 1 GeV/c protons it is −0.4682 instead of 0 in a straight cell and −0.2238 instead of 0.2443 in a cell with bends, as analytic transport and tracking establish. `etac` also loses velocity and closed-orbit time corrections: its straight-cell order-2 δ coefficient is 0.7470 instead of 1.185, and nonzero closed-orbit longitudinal advance corrupts its value. Protons and ions are most affected; ultrarelativistic electron errors are small.

title: Row 2 of the first table column reuses row 1's cache
summary: When the first column of a `twiss` table reads the per-row optics cache, for example with `base_cols=[]` or a custom `base_cols` starting with an optics column, row 2 of that column repeats row 1. Each row must describe its own sample, and drift transport of the start values, β(s) = β₀ − 2α₀s + γ₀s², gives the expected value. In a lattice of thin quadrupoles and 1 m drifts, `beta1` at s = 1 m reads 1.529 m, the value at s = 0, instead of 3.441 m, while the `alpha1` column of the same call is correct. The default `base_cols` start with `"index"`, which does not use the cache, so default tables are unaffected.

title: The spin Lie bracket uses the result field instead of the second input
summary: For vector fields with spin, written as (orbital part, spin quaternion), NonlinearNormalForm's in-place Lie bracket `lb!` uses the result field G instead of the second input H in its spin part, so the bracket is not antisymmetric. The commutator of the package's own Lie operators, and the bracket in Forest's FPP, require the term H·∇f where the code computes G·∇f. For F = (0, x·i) and H = (∂ₓ, 0), the spin component [F,H].q₁ is 0 instead of −1, and for generic polynomial fields the spin part is off by 5.0 in norm while the orbital part is exact. `lb!` is unexported, and its only caller, the correction step of `log`, changes only how fast `log` converges, so no public output is known to change.

title: Spin normal form gives NaN for an exactly vertical (or absent) spin rotation
summary: NonlinearNormalForm's spin normal form throws `InexactError: Float64(NaN + NaN*im)` when the closed-orbit spin axis is exactly vertical or there is no spin rotation. The step that aligns the axis with ŷ divides by a zero axis norm or transverse axis length, although these maps admit a normal form and Forest's FPP handles them explicitly. For a synthetic map that rotates spin by 0.6 rad about ŷ, tilting the axis by 1e-9 rad returns the correct spin-tune magnitude 0.09549 but leaves a transverse quaternion component of 2.96e-10, because the alignment angle loses the tilt. The public `twiss(spin=true)` fails in checked planar rings and straight cells, including RF and coasting cases; the thick-bend quickstart ring escapes only through transverse round-off of order 1e-34.

title: Batched Newton returns the previous iterate's `f` and `jac`
summary: BatchSolve's batched `newton` returns stale `f` and `jac` for lanes (problems in the batch) that the relative-step test accepts in the final iteration: it updates the iterate, then exits before recomputing the promised final residual and Jacobian. For x² − 2 from x = 1 with `reltol = 0.4`, the accepted iterate is 1.5, but the returned residual and Jacobian are −1.000 and 2.000 instead of 0.2500 and 3.000; the non-batched solver returns the latter values. By source inspection, batched closed-orbit finding uses this path and experimental aperture code reads the Jacobian as I − M, with M the one-turn matrix.

title: Allocating `newton`/`brent` document caller mutation they do not do
summary: The docstrings of BatchSolve's allocating `newton` and `brent` say that the returned solution `u` is the caller's `x`, mutated in place, but both work on a copy and leave `x` unchanged. Code that follows the docstring and reads `x` after the call gets the initial guess. The allocating behavior itself is sensible; only the documentation is wrong.

title: NAFF's Gram–Schmidt step is conjugated and unnormalized
summary: FundamentalFrequencies' `naff` (Numerical Analysis of Fundamental Frequencies) uses a conjugated, unnormalized Gram–Schmidt projection, corrupting later spectral lines and amplitudes. Under the package's own inner product, removing an earlier basis signal Uⱼ from Uᵢ requires the coefficient ⟨Uᵢ,Uⱼ⟩/⟨Uⱼ,Uⱼ⟩, and a corrected projection restores orthogonality. For 513 samples over 512 intervals with frequencies 0.2134, 0.2179 and 0.3171 cycles per sample and amplitudes 1, 0.6 and 0.02, the third reported line rediscovers the first and has zero amplitude. Correcting the projection and amplitude normalization recovers the missing 0.3171 line with amplitude 0.02000. The first two frequency estimates are unchanged by that correction, and changing `tol` has no effect.

summary: With `twiss(chrom=2)`, the default GTPSA descriptor caps each phase-space coordinate at degree 1 and so drops the squares x² and pₓ² that carry the dispersion feed-down, silently corrupting chromatic optics. In the documentation's 18 GeV/c electron FODO with sextupoles, started where the dispersion is 0.5317 m, ξₓ is +0.1220 instead of −0.06914 and `dbeta1` is −39.28 m instead of −30.65 m, and the documented matching recipe reaches a tracked ξₓ of 0.5128 instead of 1. summary: `twiss` builds the summary tunes and the `phi` phase-advance columns by adding the principal phase angle, in (−½, ½] turn, of each interval between sampled rows, so an interval longer than half a turn aliases the integer part. title: Reading a monomial the descriptor does not hold terminates the process
summary: In GTPSA, reading the coefficient of a monomial that the descriptor does not hold ends the Julia process from the C library with the message `invalid monomial`, with no Julia exception or stack trace; code in `catch`, `finally` and `atexit` never runs. An out-of-range indexing call should throw a catchable exception, and GTPSA's own validity test `mad_desc_isvalidm` already identifies such monomials. For t = (x + y)² under `Descriptor([1,1,1], 2)`, whose per-variable caps of 1 exclude every square, `t[[1,1,0]]` correctly returns 2.000, but `t[[2,0,0]]` ends the session with exit status 1. Per-variable caps, such as those of the default `twiss(chrom=2)` descriptor, make such reads easy to issue; by source reading, the monomial setter lacks the same check.

summary: `getterm` returns 0.0 for coefficients of the summary tunes, `etac` and `alphac` that the descriptor admits but the normal form never computes, because its guard checks only the requested monomial. summary: `getterm(q; as_taylor_series=true)` with all exponents zero, which returns a tune, `etac` or `alphac` as a Taylor series in the knobs (parameters such as quadrupole strengths), keeps the dependence on the knobs but drops the constant term. title: `copy!` into a `VectorField` drops the spin part, so `log` never corrects its spin generator
summary: NonlinearNormalForm's `copy!` omits a `VectorField` destination's quaternion, its spin part, so copies and typed conversions lose spin and `log` never receives its spin correction. title: `twiss` with `h` columns and `spin=true` ends the process (division by a zero quaternion)
summary: On rings where spin optics succeeds, requesting `h<ijkl>` columns (resonance driving terms) with `spin=true` ends the Julia process while `twiss` builds the Hamiltonian. The temporary linear map built there has a zero quaternion, and inverting it divides by zero in the native library, which bypasses Julia exception handling. summary: `twiss(bl; v0=guess)` hands the caller's matrix to the in-place closed-orbit solver, which overwrites it with the closed orbit, although the `twiss` docstring calls `v0` an initial guess and does not mention the overwrite. `find_closed_orbit` documents this mutation; documenting the overwrite in `twiss` or removing it settles the contract question. summary: With a valid TPSA definition `init`, NonlinearNormalForm's `VectorField` keyword constructor throws `MethodError: no method matching length(::Nothing)` whenever the orbital rays `v` are omitted. title: `TPSAMap` composition transports covariance at the wrong expansion point
summary: When NonlinearNormalForm composes stochastic `TPSAMap`s, which carry a noise covariance S, it transports the incoming covariance with the second map's Jacobian at that map's own expansion point instead of at the incoming orbit. First-order transport requires S₂₁ = J₂S₁J₂ᵀ + S₂, with the Jacobian J₂ evaluated at the first map's output. Translating x by 0.75 with S₁ = diag(4, 9)×10⁻¹² and then applying the shear (x, p) → (x, p + x²) returns diag(4, 9)×10⁻¹² instead of [4 6; 6 18]×10⁻¹². Re-expanding the identical shear about the incoming orbit restores the expected covariance, and an exact finite-distribution calculation agrees with it to 3.029×10⁻²⁷. Matched expansion points pass.

title: Degenerate damped modes corrupt eigenvectors and equilibrium covariance
summary: For damped maps with nonsymplectic coupling and repeated eigenvalues, NonlinearNormalForm mixes a conjugate eigenvector into the degenerate eigenspace. `mat_eigen` then returns vectors that fail the eigenvector equation, and `equilibrium_moments` violates Σ = MΣMᵀ + Q, with Σ the equilibrium covariance and Q the noise. title: Montague functions omit momentum normalization
summary: In uncoupled transverse optics, the scalar Montague chromatic functions `w`, W = √(A² + B²) built from the δ-derivatives β′ and α′ of the Twiss functions, use canonical-coordinate beta derivatives without the standard momentum normalization. With δ the relative momentum offset, the angle-coordinate beta is β_angle = (1+δ)β_c, so B requires β_c′/β_c + 1/(1+δ), and A = α_c′ − α_cB. Analytic drift transport and exact rational propagation confirm that momentum-independent angle ellipses have W = 0. For entrance (β_angle, α) = (2 m, 0.3) and (3 m, −0.2), `twiss` instead gives W = 1.044 and 1.020 initially, then 1.080 and 1.193 after 1.3 m of drift. This corrupts the chromatic-amplitude diagnostic without invalidating the canonical-coordinate beta convention itself.

title: IBS source statistics include lost particles
summary: The intrabeam scattering (IBS) kick computes the particle count, centroid and covariance that set live-particle kicks over the whole bunch, including particles marked lost. summary: With `radiation_fluctuations_on`, the random radiation kick in a tilted bend or a skew electrostatic separator is computed in a different rotated frame from the element's deterministic transport, distorting the energy kick and recoil direction. A tilted element must match the untilted one with coordinates rotated in and out under the same random seed; a direct kick calculation confirms the required frame. title: `twiss(spin=true)` fails when the spin axis is exactly vertical
summary: `twiss(spin=true)` fails for a ring whose closed-orbit spin axis is exactly vertical, because the normal-form step that aligns this axis divides by zero. In a flat ring the one-turn spin motion is a regular rotation about the vertical by 2π·aγ, where a is the magnetic anomaly and γ the Lorentz factor, and directly tracked spin quaternions agree with that analytic rotation. For electrons with γ = 100.0 in a ring of 40 identical combined-function bends, spin Twiss throws `InexactError` instead of returning a spin tune of magnitude 0.1160. Orbital Twiss succeeds, and tilting one bend by 1.000 × 10⁻⁹ rad makes spin Twiss succeed; roundoff-sized departures from vertical can also hide the failure.

title: `DAMap` keyword constructor cannot infer `nv` without `v`
summary: Constructing a `DAMap` with keywords fails when neither `nv`, the number of orbital variables, nor the orbital rays `v` are given. The constructor promises to infer `nv` from the other supplied data or from its default, but afterwards overwrites that inference with `length(v)`, which fails when `v` is `nothing`. With a six-variable, first-order GTPSA (truncated power series) descriptor, passing a 6×6 identity matrix as `v_matrix`, a six-entry reference vector `v0`, or no orbital data raises `MethodError` instead of constructing a map, while the same calls with `nv=6` succeed. summary: The postprocessing helper `track_spin`, which applies tracked spin quaternions to initial spins, accepts an initial-spin matrix of the wrong shape and silently returns wrong spins that are not unit vectors. title: Degenerate automatic z bounds misplace the cathode image
summary: When every particle has the same longitudinal position z, the automatic `Mesh3D` bounds misplace the mirror image that `solve!(at_cathode=true)` uses to model a conducting cathode plane. Electrostatics puts an equal and opposite image charge at the mirror point across the cathode plane, and a mesh with consistent manual bounds reproduces that analytic field. For 1.000 nC at 100.0 µm from the cathode on a 32³ mesh, the computed axial field is 1.401 times the correct value, matching an image 31.00 µm closer than it should be. summary: The Julia AGS spin-ramp example notebook compresses its plotted time axis and omits a factor 1/(2π) from the resonance-crossing rate, so the resonance strength it infers is wrong. The notebook defines the Froissart–Stora crossing rate α as the change in spin tune Gγ (anomaly times Lorentz factor) per turn divided by 2π, and inverting the Froissart–Stora formula for synthetic data establishes the expected strength. A spin-tune ramp of 2.000 over 1000 turns is plotted as 2.000 × 10⁻⁴, and α is taken as 0.002000 instead of 0.0003183; synthetic data with resonance strength 0.01000 yield 0.02507. title: IBS statistics are taken before the element's entrance alignment and aperture
summary: The intrabeam scattering (IBS) kick takes its bunch statistics before the element's entrance alignment and aperture act, so it mixes two coordinate frames and counts particles the entrance aperture removes. Offsetting a drift cannot change collisions within the bunch, as translating the bunch itself confirms. For 200 protons at 1.000 GeV with horizontal beam size 100.0 µm, offsetting a 1.000 m drift horizontally by 10.00 µm changes the largest IBS kick by 6.131% of its aligned value instead of zero; an outlier removed by the drift's entrance aperture changes it by 66.02% of the live-only value. Horizontal offsets and entrance losses are reproduced; source inspection places the other alignment parameters on the same entrance path.

title: Sagan RF energy kicks double the leading off-axis spin rotation
summary: The `SaganCavity` RF energy kick applies two full-strength electric spin rotations, doubling the leading spin rotation of particles with transverse momentum. An independent high-precision integral of the Thomas–BMT spin equation requires the single integrated electric impulse, or half-strength rotations if it is split around the acceleration. For a proton with P₀c, the reference momentum times the speed of light, equal to three rest energies and normalized horizontal momentum 0.1300, a 2000 eV energy gain in a zero-length cavity rotates the spin by −1.136 × 10⁻⁶ rad instead of −5.682 × 10⁻⁷ rad. Public tracking agrees with the kernel, and an on-axis particle is not rotated; exact doubling is established in the weak-gain limit, not for arbitrary finite gains.

title: IBS uses canonical momenta for flight time inside a solenoid
summary: Inside a solenoid, the intrabeam scattering (IBS) kick computes flight time and particle survival from canonical transverse momenta without subtracting the solenoid vector potential. title: Rigidity sign "correction" keeps a negative rigidity for positive species
summary: Giving a positive species a negative reference rigidity `p_over_q_ref`, in the `Beamline` constructor, by assignment or by switching `species_ref` from electron to proton, logs a sign correction but keeps the negative value. Signed rigidity R obeys pc = qRc with a forward reference momentum, so R must carry the sign of the charge q; the same state requested through `pc_ref` is rejected. For a proton line given `p_over_q_ref` = −3, the stored reference is R = −3.000 T·m, `pc_ref` = −0.8994 GeV and `E_ref` = −1.300 GeV, instead of +3.000 T·m, +0.8994 GeV and +1.300 GeV. Negatively charged species are corrected; for positive species every absolute reference quantity derived from the rigidity has the wrong sign.

title: Harmonic RF frequency uses branch-global `s`, not the containing Beamline length
summary: A harmonic-number cavity's `rf_frequency` getter and its tracking setup take as circumference the branch-global end position `s` of the cavity's Beamline, which includes every upstream Beamline of the `Branch`. The documentation defines `harmon` relative to the containing Beamline's own length, and the same cavity Beamline standing alone gives exactly that frequency. For a 1 GeV/c proton in a 3 m cavity Beamline with `harmon` = 1, adding a 2 m upstream Beamline changes the frequency from 72.88 MHz to 43.73 MHz, and a 4 m one gives 31.23 MHz. title: Exported `ParticleView` cannot be constructed
summary: Constructing the exported `ParticleView(bunch, i)`, meant as a view of particle i of a `Bunch`, fails with “too many parameters for type ParticleView”: the struct declares six type parameters, but its inner constructor supplies eight, one per field, as reflection confirms. title: Aperture kernels overwrite the state of particles that are not alive
summary: Rectangular aperture tracking overwrites an already-lost particle's loss-side code when its frozen coordinates lie outside a later aperture. A particle at x = y = 0.2 m first lost at an `x2_limit = 0.1` m aperture has state 4 (`STATE_LOST_POS_X`), but a later `y2_limit = 0.1` m aperture changes it to state 6 (`STATE_LOST_POS_Y`). Source inspection shows the same missing live-particle check in the elliptical aperture kernel. Loss-side diagnostics are silently corrupted; surviving particles are unaffected.

summary: Bmad's SciBmad exporter copies an rfcavity's `phi0`, which Bmad gives in turns (rad/2π), into SciBmad's radians field and selects `PhaseRef.AboveTransition`, introducing both a scale and a sign error. title: Bmad SciBmad writer drops the last exponent digit of aperture limits
summary: Bmad's SciBmad exporter writes aperture limits through a 24-character string, dropping the final exponent digit of the 25-character number format. A nonzero limit a·10ᵉ m therefore loads as a·10ᵗ m, with t = e/10 truncated toward zero; only magnitudes in [1, 10) m keep their exponent. Half-apertures of 0.01 m, 0.3 m and 15 m load as 1 m, 3 m and 1.5 m, and a particle at x = 0.02 m passes a collimator whose intended half-aperture is 0.01 m. An independent model of the format reproduces the loaded values, and tracking confirms the missed loss. The wrong limits load without a warning.

title: `BatchParam` scalar shortcuts test `≈ 0` and `≈ 1`, dropping factors, derivatives and knobs
summary: Arithmetic between a scalar and an array-backed `BatchParam` (addition, subtraction, multiplication and batch/scalar division) takes shortcuts when the scalar is approximately 0 or 1, discarding derivatives and power-series terms. ForwardDiff multipliers at 1 lose their derivatives, zero cases depend on the signs of the zero and the derivative, and GTPSA series with scalar part 0 or 1 lose their nonconstant coefficients. For a 0.5 m quadrupole with `Kn1 = s * BatchParam([0.3, 0.6])` and initial x = 1 mm, dx/ds at s = 1 is [0, 0] instead of [−1.833×10⁻⁴, −3.583×10⁻⁴] m, which scalar tracking and finite differences recover. Float64 factors within a relative 1.490×10⁻⁸ of 1 and Float32 factors within 3.453×10⁻⁴ are ignored, and division by zero gives +∞ in every lane.

title: A ForwardDiff or GTPSA scalar combined with a Float32 `BatchParam` throws
summary: Combining a ForwardDiff `Dual` or a GTPSA power-series scalar with a Float32 array-backed `BatchParam` fails when the operation reaches scalar conversion: `Dual(2.0, 1.0) * BatchParam(Float32[1, -2])` raises a `Float32(::Dual)` method error, and a power series with constant part 2 fails conversion to Float32 the same way. title: Simultaneous magnetic-strength convention changes rescale the partner twice
summary: A magnetic strength can be set as a field (B) or normalized to rigidity (K), integrated or per unit length. Reassigning a nonzero strength its current value through a name that changes both choices at once rescales the unassigned normal or skew partner by an extra L or 1/L, where L is the element length; this self-assignment must preserve the field, as two successive single-change self-assignments do. For a proton dipole with L = 0.25 m, rigidity R = 7.3 T·m, `Bn0` = −0.21 T and `Bs0` = 0.13 T, assigning `Kn0L` its own value keeps the kick Δpx = 7.192×10⁻³ but reduces Δpy from 4.452×10⁻³, the uniform-field Lorentz-force value, to 1.113×10⁻³. A zero partner or L = 1 m hides the error.

title: Finite EHKICK bends sloped particles on the wrong radius and leaves yp unchanged
summary: A finite-length EHKICK with a nonzero kick mistracks particles with nonzero vertical slope y′: it uses total momentum to set the projected bend radius and changes horizontal slope x′ while keeping y′ fixed. A uniform vertical field conserves total and vertical momentum, requiring a helix whose radius depends on momentum perpendicular to the field, as independent Lorentz-force integrations confirm. For a 0.7 m magnet with a 0.09 rad kick, a particle 20% above reference momentum entering with x′ = 0.08 and y′ = 0.06 leaves with y′ = 0.06000 instead of 0.06054, losing 0.8842% of its vertical momentum. At 1 mrad kick and slopes, y′ is 1.500 nrad too small; particles without vertical slope are unaffected.

title: KQUAD fringes ignore the fractional strength error FSE that scales the body
summary: KQUAD scales its body's normalized gradient by 1 + FSE, where FSE is the fractional strength error, but both nonlinear fringe kicks keep the unscaled gradient K₁. A uniform field error leaves the fringe profile normalized to the central gradient unchanged, so K₁ = 5 m⁻² with FSE = 0.2 must track like K₁ = 6 m⁻² with FSE = 0, and FSE = −1 must be a plain drift. title: UKICKMAP loss compaction gives survivors extra radiation updates
summary: With classical radiation enabled in UKICKMAP, removing an out-of-map particle can apply one extra radiation update to the survivor moved into its place. Independent radiation-integral recurrences and no-loss and loss-last controls establish the extra update.

title: RFCA subtracts its CHANGE_T clock-wrap interval once per kick
summary: In an RFCA with CHANGE_T = 1, a nonzero interval T of whole RF periods is subtracted at each of N integration kicks but added to the clock only once. summary: An RFCA with CHANGE_T = 1 removes whole periods of its own RF, a time T, from every particle's arrival time and banks it in a clock; the manual promises that cavities at non-harmonic frequencies f receive a compensating phase 2πfT. summary: With spin tracking enabled, a SOLE solenoid rotates each spin once about its longitudinal field at the exit slopes, so off-axis or sloped particles miss both the precession along their rotating trajectory in the body and the spin rotations by the radial edge fields that the orbital matrix includes. title: CSBEND with EXPAND_HAMILTONIAN=1 scales its quantum excitation by the integration order
summary: A CSBEND with EXPAND_HAMILTONIAN=1 and ISR=1 gives every radiation kick the step length s/3, although integration orders 2, 4 and 6 have 1, 3 and 7 kicks per step of length s. The energy-spread variance σδ² it adds in tracking is therefore 1/3 of the correct value at order 2 and 7/3 at order 6, and moments_output, which always integrates at order 6, applies 7/3 at every order. For a 0.9 m, 0.07 rad bend at 2.555 GeV, moments_output gives σδ² = 4.446×10⁻¹² instead of the Sands quantum-diffusion value 1.905×10⁻¹², which the exact Hamiltonian reproduces. Order 4 is correct in tracking.

title: CSBEND with EXPAND_HAMILTONIAN=1 leaves the curvature term out of the path length
summary: A CSBEND with EXPAND_HAMILTONIAN=1 accumulates the path length without the leading curvature term hx, where h is the curvature and x the horizontal offset, so the bend body adds no first-order path dependence on x, the slope x′ or the momentum deviation δ. For a 1.2 m, 0.13 rad sector bend, the path-length matrix elements R51, R52 and R56 are 9.992×10⁻¹¹, 7.772×10⁻¹¹ m and −1.835×10⁻⁸ m instead of the linear sector-bend values 0.1296, 0.07789 m and 3.377×10⁻³ m, which the exact Hamiltonian reproduces. The dispersion R16 = 0.07789 m is kept, so a ring of such bends loses the momentum compaction of its bends.

title: Identical CCBENDs that share a tracking-based matrix lose the path-length reference correction
summary: When a matrix command such as twiss_output runs before tracking, identical CCBENDs reuse the first one's tracking-based matrix, the default, but not its stored path-length correction, which the default REFERENCE_CORRECTION=1 subtracts in tracking. Each later copy of an untilted CCBEND then adds its uncorrected path excess. In a line of three CCBENDs with L = 0.85 m, ANGLE = 0.16 rad and K₁ = 0.35 m⁻², the reference electron travels 1.534×10⁻⁵ m more than the nominal length, twice the 7.672×10⁻⁶ m excess of one uncorrected magnet; without twiss_output or without sharing the path is nominal. A design TILT makes each copy recompute its correction, so tilted CCBENDs are not affected.

title: CSBEND edge model 5 adds a constant path offset and drops the y² path term when K3 is small
summary: A CSBEND edge with model 5 and fringe integral |K₃/(1+δ)| < 10⁻⁵, where δ is the momentum deviation, evaluates its path-length formula with a misplaced parenthesis. Each such edge adds the constant −K₂/(2(1+δ)²) to every particle's path and drops the term −K₂y²/(2(1+δ)²), the K₃ → 0 limit of the exact formula used for larger K₃. A pure dipole's soft edge has K₃ = 0: for curvature 0.1 m⁻¹ and a 2 cm fringe, K₂ = 10⁻⁴ and each edge shortens the path by 5.000×10⁻⁵ m, and K₂ = 0.006 gives 3.000×10⁻³ m.

title: CSBEND FSE_CORRECTION cancels a dipole-only strength error and a horizontal steering kick
summary: With FSE_CORRECTION=1 and edge model 2 or 4, CSBEND fits the strength correction that zeroes the exit slope with FSE_DIPOLE and XKICK still present, so the correction absorbs them. For a 0.75 m, 0.09 rad bend, adding FSE_DIPOLE = 7×10⁻⁴ to the bend with its error-free correction held fixed gives exit slope x′ = −6.287×10⁻⁵, as the same error given as FSE does with refitting, but the refitted FSE_DIPOLE run gives |x′| < 10⁻¹⁵. XKICK = 8×10⁻⁵ should give x′ = 7.984×10⁻⁵ and also gives |x′| < 10⁻¹⁵. The vertical deflection of YKICK is kept.

title: CSBEND FSE_CORRECTION is applied only after a command computes the bend's matrix
summary: CSBEND fits the FSE_CORRECTION strength adjustment only when a command such as twiss_output computes the bend's transfer matrix; a run that only tracks applies no correction and prints no warning. For an error-free 0.75 m, 0.09 rad bend with edge model 2 or 4, the corrected bend, obtained after twiss_output or by setting the fitted FSE by hand, has exit slope x′ = 0 and, with FSE_CORRECTION=1, the nominal path 0.75 m. Tracking alone gives x′ = 5.031×10⁻⁶ and a path 4.441×10⁻⁵ m shorter, so adding a twiss_output command changes the tracked orbit.

title: KQUAD with RADIAL=1 radiates from the unscaled field shape instead of the applied kick
summary: A KQUAD with RADIAL=1, a radially focusing lens, computes its classical radiation from field shapes that are not scaled by the strength K₁, so it radiates at K₁ = 0 and the loss grows with the square of N_SLICES. For a 3.066 GeV electron at (x, y) = (2, 1) mm through a 0.7 m lens, integrating the orbit and its radiation gives fractional energy losses of 0 at K₁ = 0 and 1.952×10⁻⁹ at K₁ = 1.3 m⁻²; with 32 slices Elegant gives 2.650×10⁻⁶ and 2.155×10⁻⁶. On the y = 0 plane the normal quadrupole, which exerts the same force, agrees with the integration.

title: Standing-wave RFCA kick tracking fiducializes at the first kick, so PHASE=90 is not the crest
summary: With STANDING_WAVE=1, N_KICKS > 1 and automatic phasing, RFCA takes its phase reference at the first of the N integration kicks, so PHASE=90, which the manual names the crest, is not the crest. For a half-wavelength gap (0.3747 m at 400 MHz, VOLT = 0.8 MV) and 5.110 GeV electrons, a phase scan and the closed-form sum of the same kicks put the crest at PHASE = 90°/N, with gain 512.6 keV for N = 8. PHASE=90 instead gives VOLT/N: 100.0 keV for N = 8 and 12.50 keV for N = 64. One kick, the matrix method (N_KICKS = 0) and the travelling-wave model keep the crest at PHASE=90.

title: RFCA END1_FOCUS and END2_FOCUS edge lenses omit the 1/β² factor
summary: RFCA's END1_FOCUS and END2_FOCUS edge lenses, in tracking and in the transfer matrix, have inverse focal length γ′/(2γ), where γ′ is the energy gain per length in units of mc². Integrating the radial field −(r/2)∂E_z/∂z of a hard field edge over the transit time dz/(βc) gives γ′/(2β²γ) at the local β and γ, so both lenses are too weak by the factor β². For electrons entering a 0.7 m cavity that adds 12 MeV at 1.5 MeV kinetic energy, the entrance lens is 4.262 m⁻¹ instead of 4.556 m⁻¹, 6.457% weak; at 5 MeV it is 0.8598% weak and at 20 MeV 0.06207% weak.

title: Matrix-method RFCA tracking uses a different R12 from its own transfer matrix
summary: An RFCA tracked with the default matrix method (N_KICKS = 0) and no body focusing computes R12 for momentum growing linearly along the cavity, while its own transfer matrix takes a uniform gradient, under which energy grows linearly. Conserved transverse momentum then gives R12 = L p₀(arcosh γ₁ − arcosh γ₀)/(γ₁ − γ₀), with γ₀, γ₁ the entrance and exit Lorentz factors and p₀ the entrance βγ; 1024-kick tracking approaches it within 1.568×10⁻⁶. For electrons entering a 0.7 m cavity that adds 12 MeV at 1.5 MeV kinetic energy, tracking gives R12 = 0.2229 m instead of 0.2221 m, 0.3685% too large; the error is 0.03247% at 5 MeV and 7.003×10⁻⁶ at 20 MeV.

title: RFCA with Q ramps its voltage as the square root of a stored-energy fill, not as a resonant fill
summary: An RFCA with nonzero Q, described as a cavity that charges up to its voltage from zero, ramps the voltage as VOLT·√(1 − e^(−ωt/Q)), with ω the angular RF frequency and t the time since the reference time. The envelope equation of a resonant mode driven at its frequency from rest gives VOLT·(1 − e^(−ωt/2Q)); the square-root law rises with infinite initial slope and stays above it. For a 350 MHz, 200 kV cavity with Q = 3500, the kick after 100 RF periods (285.7 ns) is 81.07 kV instead of 17.17 kV, 4.722 times too large, and 153.9 kV instead of 72.32 kV after 1.429 µs. Both laws reach VOLT in steady state.

title: Automatic CSBEND field expansion order is n+2, not the n+3 the manual states
summary: For a CSBEND with EXPANSION_ORDER=0, the manual promises field terms through total degree n+3 in transverse coordinates x and y, with a minimum degree of 4, where n is the highest nonzero multipole order. For normal sextupole (n = 2) and octupole (n = 3) components, tracking instead matches explicit order n+2. Independent vacuum-field integration validates the documented-order trajectories. In a 0.25 m bend of curvature 1 m⁻¹ with K₃ = 3000 m⁻⁴, particles starting at x = 15–30 mm and y = 20–40 mm with zero slopes acquire slope differences up to 2.823×10⁻⁷. The tested quadrupole-only and midplane controls are unaffected.

title: Unmatched alpha derivatives report phase derivatives
summary: Elegant's `twiss_output` with `matched=0` propagates user-given entrance optics through a non-periodic beamline and writes the momentum derivatives of the Twiss alpha functions, `dalphax/dp` and `dalphay/dp`. These columns instead hold the derivatives of the betatron phase, 2π times the chromaticities. For a 0.5 m quadrupole with K1 = 0.6 m⁻² followed by a 1 m drift, entering with βx = 3 m, αx = 0.4, βy = 2 m and αy = −0.3, the exact hard-edge map gives dαx/dδ = 0.004523 and dαy/dδ = 1.549, where δ is the relative momentum offset; Elegant writes −0.3591 and 0.07649. The tune and beta derivatives are correct.

title: Cubic compaction omits momentum–transverse quadratic terms
summary: Elegant's `twiss_output` computes the third-order momentum compaction αc3 of a periodic cell but leaves out the path-length terms in which the momentum offset δ multiplies a transverse coordinate that is itself driven by δ². Take a 10 m cell with betatron tunes 0.17 and 0.23, a second-order term T166 = 0.2 m (horizontal shift ∝ δ²) and a path term T561 = 0.3 (path length ∝ xδ). The closed orbit is x = 0.1 m δ², so the path length is 10 m + 0.03 m δ³ and αc3 = 0.003. Elegant writes the correct second-order dispersion 0.1 m but αc3 = 0.

title: CCBEND radiation totals omit repeated periods
summary: With `twiss_output`, `radiation_integrals=1` and `n_periods` greater than 1, Elegant adds, for CCBEND (canonical combined-function bend) elements, the integrals I₁ to I₅ of one period to the totals without multiplying by `n_periods`, although the per-element contributions are multiplied. For a cell of two 1 m bends with curvature 0.1 m⁻¹ at 6000 mₑc, I₂ must be 0.02000 m⁻¹ for one period and 0.04000 m⁻¹ for two, but Elegant writes 0.02000 m⁻¹ for both. The energy loss per turn then stays at 24.88 keV instead of doubling to 49.77 keV, and the damping times double instead of staying unchanged. The same cell with SBEN bends is correct.

title: Initial moments omit shared-dispersion covariance terms
summary: With moments_output matched=0, equilibrium=0, explicit Twiss, dispersion and longitudinal inputs produce a covariance matrix Σ for (x, x′, y, y′, s, δ) missing eight terms, where s is longitudinal position and δ is relative momentum offset. For independent betatron motion, dispersion η requires cross-plane covariances ηᵢηⱼΣ₆₆ and transverse–longitudinal covariances ηᵢΣ₆₅. For longitudinal emittance ε_z = 1 μm, β_z = 4 m, α_z = 0.2, η_x = 0.1 m and η_y = −0.03 m, Σ₁₃ must be −7.800×10⁻¹⁰ m² and Σ₁₅ −2.000×10⁻⁸ m², but both are zero. Propagated covariance matrices inherit the error. Nonzero momentum spread with dispersion in both planes, or dispersion with longitudinal position–momentum correlation, triggers the error.

title: Third-order concatenation multiplies spurious path-origin terms of tracking-derived maps by the accumulated path length
summary: Elegant derives CCBEND maps by tracking, and those maps carry spurious terms that depend on the incoming path coordinate s. title: Tracking tune shift with amplitude ignores nuy_roi_width and the amplitude scaling factors
summary: In tracking mode, Elegant's `tune_shift_with_amplitude` searches the vertical tune peak within `nux_roi_width` and never reads `nuy_roi_width`, `scale_down_factor`, `scale_up_factor` or `scale_up_limit`, all documented in the manual. title: Coupling integral reads a KSEXT's YAW as its vertical offset DY
summary: Elegant's `twiss_output` coupling estimate (`couplingIntegral`, `emittanceRatio`) includes the skew gradient K2·(y − DY) of vertically displaced sextupoles, but for a KSEXT it reads DY through the SEXT data layout, where the KSEXT stores its YAW. title: moments_output mode emittances normalize the (s, δ) pair with the transverse sign
summary: Elegant's `moments_output` computes the mode emittances e1, e2 and e3 by normalizing the one-turn eigenvectors with the same symplectic sign for all three coordinate pairs, but its longitudinal pair (s, δ) needs the opposite sign, because the canonical coordinate conjugate to δ is −s. title: rf_setup sets the electron's synchronous phase for positrons and protons
summary: After `change_particle` selects a positron or a proton, `rf_setup` gives the RFCA and MODRF cavities the electron's synchronous phase, although these cavities reverse the energy gain of positively charged particles. The positron's cavity then removes the radiation loss per turn U₀ instead of replacing it, and the synchrotron motion of either species grows exponentially. title: WAKE cache substitutes the first requested column pair
summary: When two WAKE elements in one Elegant run select different wake columns (WCOLUMN) or time columns (TCOLUMN) from the same table file, the second element silently reuses the first element's columns, because the table is cached by file name alone. For a table with kernels A and B = 3A, the earliest particles of a 12-electron, 2 nC bunch should lose the sum of both kernels, 8000 eV; the shared file gives 4000 eV (A applied twice) or 12000 eV (B applied twice), depending on element order, which is an error of −50% or +50%. A byte-identical copy of the table under another file name gives the correct result.

title: Broadband ZTRANSVERSE doubles its DC impedance
summary: Broadband ZTRANSVERSE sets its zero-frequency impedance to 2Rₛ/Q instead of the documented Rₛ/Q, where Rₛ is the shunt impedance and Q the resonator quality factor. This adds a constant transverse wake over the finite Fourier-transform window for beams with a net transverse offset. For 12 electrons at 50 mₑc, 2 nC total charge and 1 mm horizontal offset in adjacent 50 ps bins, with Rₛ = 1×10⁶ Ω/m, Q = 1, resonant frequency 1 GHz and 8192 bins, the leading group's kick is 6.960×10⁻⁶ rad instead of the independently summed 6.769×10⁻⁶ rad. The excess is 1.911×10⁻⁷ rad per particle and halves when the window doubles.

title: BEAMBEAM kicks change arrival time because s is not rescaled
summary: A BEAMBEAM kick changes momentum but leaves the stored longitudinal coordinate s = βct unchanged, where t is arrival time, c is the speed of light and β is speed divided by c. The output time therefore changes by the ratio of incoming to outgoing speed, although the zero-length element must preserve time and rescale s. For an electron of momentum 1 mₑc at horizontal position x = 0.2300 mm, a 1.300 nC uniform opposing bunch of radius 1.300 mm changes an input time of 1 µs by −1.936×10⁻¹¹ s, a relative error of −1.936×10⁻⁵. Zero input time masks the error.

title: Dipole resonators create momentum in the disabled plane
summary: When TRFMODE or FTRFMODE tracks a dipole mode in one plane only, its longitudinal kick creates momentum in the other plane in proportion to the incoming slope there. The code updates longitudinal momentum p∥ before recovering incoming transverse momenta from slopes. For a horizontal mode the voltage is independent of vertical position, so vertical momentum pᵧ must be conserved. For 16 electrons with momentum 750 mₑc, horizontal and vertical slopes (0.01200, 0.02400), horizontal offset 8.000 mm and charge 0.7000 nC, the last particle's vertical momentum instead changes by Δpᵧ = −7.165×10⁻⁴ mₑc, matching vertical slope times Δp∥ within 10⁻¹⁴ mₑc.

title: Later SCMULT bunches use the exit beta function for the entrance weight
summary: When Elegant tracks a bunch train with SCMULT space-charge kicks (`insert_sceffects` in bunch mode), every bunch after the first integrates the space-charge strength over each element with the element's exit beta function β in place of its entrance value, so identical bunches receive different kicks. A bunch's kick depends only on its own charge distribution and the optics; the manual's linear force integrated with independently computed matched optics reproduces the first bunch's kick. Where β falls from 0.9141 m to 0.8018 m along a 0.3 m drift, the second and third of three identical bunches receive 6.542% less kick than the first, with linear and nonlinear forces alike.

title: Sliced linear SCMULT normalizes every slice by the whole-bunch beam size
summary: With constant matched optics, linear SCMULT space-charge forces, slicing on (`slice_duration` > 0), interpolation off and slice populations meeting `slice_threshold`, Elegant normalizes each slice's field gradient by the whole bunch's rms widths. title: TRWAKE quadrupole probe coordinates omit element misalignment
summary: TRWAKE quadrupole wakes (probe exponents 1, drive exponents 0) use each particle's global transverse coordinate even when the structure has misalignments DX and DY. title: SCMULT keeps stale beam sizes across zero-length elements that change them
summary: SCMULT measures the beam sizes for its space-charge strength only at exits of elements with positive length, so after a zero-length element that changes the transverse sizes, such as an EMATRIX or ROTATE, the next segment pairs the old sizes with the new beta functions. title: insert_sceffects clear leaves a negative specification count, crashing or silently dropping every SCMULT
summary: Setting clear = 1 on insert_sceffects decrements the count of insertion specifications to −1 instead of 0, so the next specification is written one entry before its array. Clearing and replacing an earlier command with the same selector then completes with no SCMULT and no warning, so the run has no space charge; clearing in a fresh run, clearing alone, and clearing with disable = 1 after an earlier command crash. The manual says clear deletes prior insertions and disable makes a command ignored, so each run must complete, and all but the lone clear must insert one SCMULT. In a one-segment ring with a 0.8000 nC bunch, the replacement's expected linear slope kick of 2.379×10⁻⁴ becomes exactly zero.

title: CSRCSBEND with LINEARIZE=1 mixes arrival time with path length, applies ETILT twice and drops SYNCH_RAD
summary: CSRCSBEND with LINEARIZE=1 replaces the integrator by a linear matrix, but applies the matrix's path-length row to the arrival time c t, includes ETILT both in the matrix and in the element's misalignment transform, and skips the classical radiation requested by SYNCH_RAD=1. title: WAKE gives each particle the full W(0) of its own bin, so full-origin wakes such as CORGPIPE's overstate the loss
summary: WAKE gives every particle the table's W(0) times all charge in its own time bin, its own included. When W(0) is the wake just behind a charge, W(0⁺), as in CORGPIPE's table, built from Bane's model, a charge should receive W(0⁺)/2 from itself and nothing from charge behind it (beam-loading theorem), so the mean loss is too large by W(0⁺)/2 times the average charge of a particle's bin. title: ibsEmittance stops the equilibrium emittance at ε₀/(1+κ) when τx > τy and reports convergence
summary: ibsEmittance, run for equilibrium emittances at coupling ratio κ = εy/εx, never returns a horizontal emittance below ε₀/(1+κ), with ε₀ the uncoupled natural emittance. When the horizontal damping time τx exceeds the vertical τy (horizontal damping partition Jx < 1) and IBS is weak, the radiation–IBS balance the program solves has its root below that bound, at ε₀/(1+κτx/τy) without IBS; the program returns the bound and reports "Emittance converged". For a 3 GeV, 55.20 m ring with Jx = 0.8029 and κ = 0.1, the returned emittance is 2.232% above the root at 10⁻¹² nC and at 1 nC, and the balance misses zero by 2.232% of its excitation term. Rings with τx ≤ τy are not affected.

title: IBSCATTER uses the electron's classical radius and mass for every species
summary: After change_particle selects a muon, a proton or a custom species, IBSCATTER computes its intrabeam-scattering growth rates with the electron's classical radius and mass, and so reports and applies the electron rates of the same beam. At fixed velocity, geometric phase space and particle count, the Bjorken–Mtingwa rate scales as r_c² ln Λ, with r_c the classical radius and ln Λ the Coulomb logarithm; for protons this is 4.106×10⁻⁷ of the electron rate. For a 1 nC beam at βγ = 30, the element gives protons a longitudinal rate of 8.067 s⁻¹, 2.436×10⁶ times the correct 3.312×10⁻⁶ s⁻¹. The IBS computed by moments_output is a separate calculation that uses the species' classical radius.

title: moments_output IBS Coulomb logarithm mixes electron-unit momenta with the species mass
summary: After change_particle selects a muon or a custom heavy species, moments_output with ibs_iterations forms the Coulomb logarithm ln Λ of its intrabeam-scattering (IBS) diffusion from momentum spreads in electron units but a classical minimum impact parameter with the species mass M, which inflates that cutoff by (M/mₑ)². Where it exceeds the other cutoff, ln Λ and the IBS diffusion, proportional to it, are too small. The correct value follows from Kubo and Oide's cutoffs in physical units on the same beam moments. In a radiating test ring at normalized momentum βγ = 1200 with 1 pC, ln Λ is 12.76–18.63% low for muons and 86.64–95.11% low for antiprotons, a custom species. Electrons and positrons are not affected.

title: Touschek scattering rates use the electron's classical radius for every species
summary: After change_particle selects a muon, a proton or a custom species, touschek_scatter computes the Touschek scattering rates at TSCATTER elements with the electron's classical radius rₑ instead of the species' r_c = q²/(4πε₀Mc²). At fixed βγ, beam geometry, particle count and momentum aperture, Piwinski's rate scales as r_c², so the correct rate for a singly charged species is the electron's times (mₑ/M)²; Elegant instead writes the electron's rates, from Piwinski's formula and from the Monte Carlo, 4.275×10⁴ times too large for muons and 3.372×10⁶ for protons. For a 1 nC beam at βγ = 100 with a ±10⁻³ momentum aperture, it reports 5.375×10¹¹ s⁻¹ for protons against 1.594×10⁵ s⁻¹ from an independent evaluation of Piwinski's formula.

title: moments_output IBS uses a negative particle count for positrons and protons
summary: After change_particle selects positrons or protons, moments_output with ibs_iterations divides the bunch charge by Elegant's internal particle charge, negative for these species, so its intrabeam-scattering (IBS) calculation uses a negative particle count. With the default automatic Coulomb logarithm ln Λ, the beam density is negative, and ln Λ and every moment are NaN from the first IBS update, without warning. A prescribed ln Λ reverses the IBS diffusion. By charge conjugation, a positron ring with the RF phase shifted by 180° must reproduce the electron result: in a 524.8 m ring at 1.5 GeV/c with 1 nC and ln Λ = 10, IBS raises the mode emittance e₁ from 6.604 to 8.742 nm for electrons, but positrons get 6.599 nm.

title: touschek_scatter Monte Carlo rate does not converge when the momentum aperture lies inside the sampled energy spread
summary: touschek_scatter samples the incoming beam out to distribution_cutoff (3 by default) times the rms energy spread σδ and counts every outgoing particle beyond the momentum aperture δm, including particles that were already beyond it. When δm lies inside the sampled spread, nearly forward collisions of those particles, whose Møller cross section is limited only by the sampled angle range, dominate: the Monte Carlo rate SLocalRate grows with n_simulated instead of converging, and a few particles carry the loss weights. With δm = 0.5σδ, SLocalRate is 9.372×10¹², 2.687×10¹³ and 1.395×10¹⁴ s⁻¹ for 2×10⁴, 2×10⁵ and 2×10⁶ samples, against 1.030×10¹⁰ s⁻¹ from Piwinski's formula. With δm = 31.25σδ it is within 1.748% of Piwinski's rate.

title: Pelegant fails to load a multi-page beam file when a later page leaves a worker without rows
summary: When Pelegant, Elegant's MPI version, loads several particle-file pages with `track_pages_separately=0`, it should combine them into one beam. If a later page gives no rows to a worker that read an earlier page, the run stops with "Unable to get column--no rows left" before tracking. A five-particle file split into pages of four and one fails on three ranks (two workers), whereas serial Elegant and Pelegant with a one-plus-four split return all five particles unchanged.

title: SDDS Gill–Miller integral of a three-sample table is zero and leaves a result unset
summary: When `sddsprocess` computes a `gmintegral` from three samples, or a program calls the SDDS routine `GillMillerIntegration` with three samples, the final integral silently becomes zero. For f = 1 at x = 0, 1, 2 the correct integral is 2; for f = x at x = 0.2, 0.7, 2.3 it is 2.625, yet the utility returns 0 for both without warning. Direct library calls also leave the middle cumulative result unwritten, while four-sample constant and nonuniform cubic controls agree with exact antiderivatives to double precision roundoff.

title: SDDS complete elliptic integral E(k) returns π/4 at the endpoints k = ±1
summary: Evaluating the complete elliptic integral of the second kind, E(k) = ∫₀^{π/2} √(1 − k² sin²θ) dθ, with `sddsprocess` (rpn `cei2`) or the SDDS routines `E_cei` and `KE_cei` returns π/4 = 0.7854 at k = ±1. At those endpoints the integrand is cos θ and E = 1, so the result is 21.46% too small, without a utility warning. At the six tested interior moduli, results agree with an independent implementation within 2×10⁻¹⁵; at k = 0.8, E = 1.276.

title: SDDS moment accumulation discards the earlier batches
summary: The SDDS routines `accumulateMoments` and `accumulateWeightedMoments` return the mean, rms and standard deviation of data supplied in batches (first call with reset = 1, later calls with reset = 0), but in their default single-thread form they do not combine the batches. For the values 2, 4, 8, 10 supplied as [2, 4] then [8, 10], the mean is 6, the rms √46 = 6.782 and the sample standard deviation √(40/3) = 3.651, as one call over all four values gives. The unweighted routine returns a mean of 4.5 (the last batch's sum over the total count) and the unit-weight routine returns 9 (the last batch's mean).

title: The manual's bunch-input example assigns particle IDs 2001–3000 to bunch 1 instead of bunch 2
summary: The manual says that with `IDSlotsPerBunch` S the bunch of particle ID I is ⌊(I − 1)/S⌋, then illustrates this for S = 1000 with IDs 1 to 1000 in bunch 0 and IDs 2001 to 3000 in bunch 1. The formula, which the code implements, puts IDs 1001 to 2000 in bunch 1 and IDs 2001 to 3000 in bunch 2. A user who follows the example, leaving out IDs 1001 to 2000, and selects bunch 1 of a transverse wake gets no kick on any particle; in the test, the 1.252×10⁻⁷ rad kick that the example implies for particle 3000 appears only when bunch 2 is selected.
